headline: A US map puts African countries in the wrong places

sources.title: State Department apologizes for Africa map that mislabeled countries
State Dept. apologizing for Africa map that mislabeled every country
US government mislabels countries on map of Africa at global conference
US' Africa Map Blunder At AIDS Conference Triggers Global Backlash | Firstpost Live | 4K (video, Firstpost)

chunks.text: At a large international [[conference]] on AIDS in Rio de Janeiro on July 26, the United States [[State Department]] {{put up}} a [[slide]] showing a map of Africa. Nigeria had been placed in the Sahara [[desert]]. Mozambique had {{shifted across to}} the Horn of Africa. Ivory Coast was on the wrong side of the [[continent]]. The [[borders]] were drawn as soft shapes that matched no real country.

verbs.wrong: To prepare slides before a talk

verbs.correct: To move over to another place
verbs.wrong: To be drawn much larger than it is

chunks.text: The [[audience]] {{picked up on}} it [[at once]]. The room was full of doctors, researchers and health [[officials]] from across Africa, and many of them work in the countries that had been moved. A [[watermark]] on the image suggested the map had been produced by an AI tool, and the slide appeared to have been {{thrown together}} shortly before the [[session]] began. The State Department later called it an [[unfortunate]] [[error]] and apologized to its African [[partners]].

chunks.text: The story {{caught on}} quickly because of when it happened. The same conference heard that international [[funding]] for HIV has {{dropped off}} [[sharply]], down 18 percent, which is the [[steepest]] fall in about twenty years. [[Delegates]] who had spent the week listening to promises of [[partnership]] then watched their own countries {{shuffled around}} a map by a machine. Several said afterwards that [[carelessness]] of this kind carries a message whether anyone [[intends]] it or not.

verbs.wrong: To be shown on television news

chunks.text: The map itself was small and was quickly {{taken down}}. What people at the conference kept {{coming back to}} was the habit behind it, which is {{handing over}} a job to software and then {{signing off on}} the result without reading it. As one delegate [[put it]], if nobody in that room could {{make out}} where their own country was, somebody should have checked before the slide ever {{went up}}.

tf.s: The State Department put up a map of Africa at a conference in Rio de Janeiro on July 26.
tf.why: At a large international conference on AIDS in Rio de Janeiro on July 26, the United States State Department put up a slide showing a map of Africa.

tf.s: On the map, Nigeria had been placed correctly on the west coast.
tf.why: Nigeria had been placed in the Sahara desert, Mozambique had shifted across to the Horn of Africa, and Ivory Coast was on the wrong side of the continent.

tf.s: The audience picked up on the mistake at once.
tf.why: The audience picked up on it at once. The room was full of doctors, researchers and health officials from across Africa.

tf.s: International funding for HIV has dropped off sharply, down 18 percent.
tf.why: The same conference heard that international funding for HIV has dropped off sharply, down 18 percent, which is the steepest fall in about twenty years.

tf.s: The State Department defended the map and refused to apologize.
tf.why: The State Department later called it an unfortunate error and apologized to its African partners.

tf.s: The map stayed on the screen for the rest of the conference.
tf.why: The map itself was small and was quickly taken down.
